dek: The Studio Museum's "Geometries" is up, MoMA PS1's "Hard Art" opens Thursday, and ten artists are in both.

slides.label: Two shows
slides.text: Uptown, the Studio Museum in Harlem has *"Geometries"* on its walls. This Thursday, Nov. 5, MoMA PS1 in Queens opens *"Hard Art,"* built around abstract painting by Black artists from 1969 to today.

slides.label: Uptown
slides.text: Thelma Golden curated "Geometries" with Simon Ghebreyesus. The museum lists *30 artists*, from Alma Thomas, Norman Lewis and Jack Whitten to *Julie Mehretu*, Stanley Whitney and Adam Pendleton.

slides.label: The idea
slides.text: The museum frames geometry as more than math: lines and shapes that carry emotion, identity and sacred knowledge, drawn from city maps to *West African textiles*. Al Loving: *"even a box can be a self-portrait."*

slides.label: The building
slides.text: The Studio Museum reopened its *82,000-square-foot* home on West 125th Street in November 2025 after a seven-year closure. In September, Beyoncé announced a *$2 million* gift. Sunday admission is *free*.

slides.label: Queens
slides.text: "Hard Art" brings together *40-plus artists* across three generations, from Frank Bowling, Howardena Pindell and Sam Gilliam to Aria Dean and Torkwase Dyson. It runs through *March 2027*.

slides.label: The history
slides.text: The title comes from Peter Bradley's description of "The DeLuxe Show." PS1 also ties it to *"Afro-American Abstraction,"* curated by April Kingsley at PS1 in *1980*. A return visit, 46 years later.

slides.label: Ten names
slides.text: By the Den's count, *ten artists* appear in both shows, including Jack Whitten, Julie Mehretu, Al Loving and Adam Pendleton. Nobody announced a joint project. That shows where *the canon is moving*.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Do both, the same week if possible: a free Sunday in Harlem, then PS1, *free since January 2026*. Bring the friend who "doesn't get" abstract art. That person is *who these shows are for*.

question: Black abstraction season: HARLEM first or QUEENS first? Pick one.

caption_instagram:
Abstraction got sold as the art with no address. This fall, Harlem and Queens are giving it two.

The Studio Museum in Harlem has "Geometries" up now, curated by Thelma Golden with Simon Ghebreyesus: 30 artists, from Alma Thomas and Jack Whitten to Julie Mehretu and Adam Pendleton. This Thursday, Nov. 5, MoMA PS1 opens "Hard Art," more than 40 artists across three generations of Black abstraction since 1969, organized by Connie Butler with Sheldon Gooch and running through March 2027. PS1 ties the show to "Afro-American Abstraction," curated by April Kingsley at PS1 in 1980. By our count from the museums' own lists, ten artists appear in both shows. Nobody announced it as a joint project.

Sunday admission at the Studio Museum is free, and PS1 has been free since January 2026.

Two of New York's major institutions are independently making the same argument this season.

The Studio Museum in Harlem's "Geometries," curated by Thelma Golden, presents 30 artists who treat geometry as a carrier of identity and meaning. On Thursday, Nov. 5, MoMA PS1 opens "Hard Art," a 40-plus-artist survey of abstract painting by Black artists in the United States from 1969 to today, running through March 2027.

By the Den's count, ten artists appear in both exhibitions without any announced coordination. That kind of overlap is a strong signal of where curatorial attention, and the canon, is moving.
